column1: # Shared fixture for keys.awk and keys.ps1. One case per line:
# The mode is bash or pwsh. In the command, \n is a newline and \t a tab. The
# expected keys are the extractor's output lines, each written <segment>:<entry>
# and joined with " | ", or "-" for no output. Read by gate-test.sh and
# gate-test.ps1, so a case added here is checked against both extractors.
# Plain commands: the first word, then the subcommand candidates, then the task
# names below each key, which only a PROJECT class reads.

column3: 1:git | 1:git status | 1:git commit | 1:git status commit | 1:+git status | 1:+git commit | 1:+git status commit

1:svn | 1:svn info | 1:svn status | 1:svn commit | 1:svn info status | 1:svn info commit | 1:svn status commit | 1:+svn info | 1:+svn status | 1:+svn commit | 1:+svn info status | 1:+svn info commit | 1:+svn status commit | 1:+svn info status commit
1:gh | 1:gh pr | 1:gh pr create | 1:+gh pr | 1:+gh create | 1:+gh x | 1:+gh y | 1:+gh pr create | 1:+gh pr x | 1:+gh pr y | 1:+gh pr create x | 1:+gh pr create y

column2: make a b c d e f g h i

column1: # A word that cannot be read as a name adds the marker "?" at its depth.
# A word directly after a flag is read as that flag's value when it cannot be
# read as a name, so it adds no marker.
# Paths as the first word are keys as written.
# A quoted or odd first word goes to the reader.
# Leading assignments, redirections, shell words, and wrappers are dropped.

column2: FOO=1 sudo -E env BAR=2 nohup git push
if git diff --quiet; then echo same; fi
for f in a b; do rm "$f"; done

column1: # Comments, with a quote in them.
# Separators, and the redirections that are not separators.
# Single-quoted text is skipped when looking for substitutions: a commit
# message's Markdown backticks are not commands.
# A substitution inside double quotes is read (R8).
